P01-001.device_notes: Whole-chapter span (28 verses), well above the 7-10 typical density; the length is disclosed as a fact, is no ground for the grade, and no internal cut is forced where the bytes mark none. The grade rests on the close seam: at 1:28 the throne vision ends on a narrative close with no close-role formula (the prophet sees the glory, falls on his face and hears a voice), a discernible close whose near face is weaker than a formula would make it, while across the seam 2:1 opens with 'he said to me' inside the vision and turns to the commission; whether the vision closes at 1:28 or runs on into the commission is an open question of this stretch, and the samekh after 1:28 (single witness) corroborates the paragraph without deciding it. MT 1:3 is cited only under the 49-verse any-form word-event count, never blended with the 48-verse first-person family. K/Q at 1:8 checked before quoting: the unit does not splice the disputed word. The OSHB editorial note at 1:11 is disclosed as single-witness apparatus, not a reading change. Paseq at 1:1 and 1:27 disclosed count-only (single-witness); no intra-verse position is claimed.

P01-007.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:22 וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.3.22) (“Yahweh’s hand was there on me” (web:Ezek.3.22)), the hand-of-YHWH construct read here as a genuine vision onset (contrast oshb:Ezek.3.14, where the construct accompanies the spirit carrying the prophet away, a transit rather than a new scene) because it opens a fresh scene: “Arise, go out into the plain” (web:Ezek.3.22). 3:25 announces that עֲבוֹתִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.3.25) ('ropes') will be put on the prophet; the word recurs at 4:8 in the siege sign-act, across the 3:27/4:1 seam (the same consonants and vowels under a different accent), so the muteness command and the sign-acts share a device, and that continuity is weighed here against the seam even though the unit boundary stands. 3:26 carries the fifth rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה. Close: 3:27, הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.27) (“He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house” (web:Ezek.3.27)) - the sixth verse in chapters 2-3 to name the rebellious house (sweep: 12 verses book-wide name it, six of them in chapters 2-3), and the close of the book's opening collection (chapters 1-3); a samekh is recorded after this verse. Across the seam, 4:1 opens with וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.1) ('and you, son of man'), quoted byte for byte as the 3:27 clause is, and turns to the command to take a tile, the sub-onset that starts the sign-acts. The unit therefore stops at 3:27 and does not extend into 4:1; the seam's near side is closed by the refrain and the samekh after 3:27 (single witness), and its far side is opened by that sub-onset.
P01-007.strongest_rejected_alternative: Placing the seam between the book's first two collections at 3:15/3:16 instead of 3:27/4:1, on the strength of 3:16's own strict word-event and the seven-day close it answers. Weighed on the bytes, the onset side of that seam is strong: 3:16 sets מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16)) before its strict word-event, and a pe follows 3:16 itself (single witness), after the word-event verse rather than before it. Its close side is narrative: 3:15 ends the journey to the exiles on seven days of sitting among them, a report rather than a refrain. The rebellious-house refrain runs on both sides of 3:16 (sweep: of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house, four stand before 3:16 and two after it), so a parent seam there would divide that series, whereas at 3:27/4:1 the series' sixth verse stands on the close side and the sub-onset of 4:1 on the onset side. The alternative is kept as a held question and not argued away, because the ropes of 3:25, taken up at 4:8, tie the muteness command (3:22-27) to the sign-acts (4:1-17) across the later seam.
P01-007.device_notes: Category deviation disclosed: this span also reads as a commission narrative (the muteness charge proper runs 3:24-3:27 inside this vision-opened scene); it is classed with the vision reports because the unit's onset device is the hand-of-YHWH construct at 3:22. Paseq at 3:27 occurs twice (double occurrence on one verse), disclosed count-only, single-witness. The ropes word shared by 3:25 and 4:8 is disclosed as continuity across the 3:27/4:1 seam; it argues for the closeness of the two units, while the refrain close at 3:27 and the sub-onset at 4:1 keep the seam between them. The witness records a samekh after MT 3:21 (single witness), on the far side of this unit's onset seam, where it corroborates the onset without deciding it.

P01-012.boundary_rationale: Onset: 7:1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.7.1) (“Moreover Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.7.1)), a strict word-event textually identical to 6:1's formula, a hard seam. Close: 7:4, וִידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.7.4) (“Then you will know that I am Yahweh” (web:Ezek.7.4)), the 2mp wider-family recognition close, with a pe recorded after it, before 7:5 reopens with a fresh messenger formula on the same 'end' theme.

P03-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Classifying 16:59-63 as the close of the chapter's parable-allegory rather than a separate salvation-oracle row was weighed and not taken: the covenant-establishment promise ('I will establish for you an everlasting covenant') is a restoration burden distinct in kind from the accusation and sentence that fill the rest of the chapter, and it opens with its own messenger formula rather than continuing the sisters comparison; that deviation from the chapter's otherwise uniform category is disclosed here.
P03-009.device_notes: Category deviation disclosed: this row is classed as a salvation oracle rather than as part of the parable-allegory although it sits inside MT 16, because the covenant-establishment promise opening at 16:59 carries its own messenger formula and turns from the sisters' indictment to YHWH's remembered covenant, so this restoration burden is cut off from the accusation that precedes it. MT 16:59 Ketiv/Qere single note disclosed above. A samekh is set after MT 16:58 (single witness); that front-seam break divides the sisters' sentence from the covenant turn this row opens.

P03-015.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:5 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְאִ֖ישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.5) ('if a man is righteous and does what is just and right'), a default case-law onset following the thesis stated at 18:4; the samekh recorded there (single witness), closing the unit before it, corroborates this row's onset from the far side of the seam. Close side: the row runs to 18:9, and its own final words are the utterance formula חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.9), a genuine verse-final refrain closing the first case before the wicked son's case opens at 18:10 with no formula of its own. That utterance is verse-final and carries no mark, and 18:10 brings no fresh onset past it, so it closes a paragraph inside the one word-event unit and not the unit itself; behind 18:5 the seam is a case turn with no formula on either face, corroborated by the samekh on 18:4 and not decided by it. Two seams of that shape are why the row is held at reduced confidence.
P03-015.strongest_rejected_alternative: No parashah mark (single witness) corroborates a seam at 18:9; keeping 18:5-9 fused with 18:10-20 into one eleven-plus-five-verse row was weighed and not taken because the utterance formula there is genuinely verse-final, unlike its four non-final recurrences elsewhere in MT 18 (18:3, 18:23, 18:30, 18:32), the one formula-marked seam inside the chapter's case law. That signature is paragraph-final where it stands, since 18:10 brings no fresh onset past it, so the ground for refusing the fusion is a paragraph-grade signal and no more; the seam is kept as a case turn inside one word-event unit, which is part of why the row is held at reduced confidence.
P03-015.device_notes: No K/Q note, no paseq, no parashah mark, and no editorial note lie within this span (single-witness apparatus).

P05-003.device_notes: Pe at 22:31 (single-witness, close of this unit). No paseq and no K/Q site lies inside 22:23-31.

P06-014.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:20 is the strict word-event formula, the whole verse וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.28.20), opening the oracle against Sidon that 28:21 commands: “Son of man, set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against it” (web:Ezek.28.21). Across that seam 28:19 ends the dirge over the king of Tyre on its refrain בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.28.19), with a pe recorded after it (single witness); neither the refrain nor the mark is one of the book's counted close formulas, so the onset rests on its near face alone. Close: 28:23 ends verse-final on the counted recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.28.23) with no mark after it, and 28:24 opens with no onset device of any kind; it turns from Sidon to the house of Israel and ends on the Adonai form of the recognition formula with a samekh after it, which belongs to the Israel coda of 28:24-26 and not to this oracle, so the close too rests on its near face alone. Both seams therefore carry a licensed signal on the near face and nothing that counts on the far face; inside the span the messenger formula of 28:22 stands within the speech that 28:21 commands and is paragraph-grade, weighed below.
P06-014.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the oracle through 28:26, so that the Israel coda 28:24-26 closes the Sidon unit: 28:24 opens with no onset device, and recognition formulas stand at 28:22, 28:23, 28:24 and 28:26, so no formula-marked onset separates the coda from what precedes it. Weighed and not taken: 28:23 closes the Sidon oracle verse-final on the recognition formula, 28:24 turns from Sidon to the house of Israel, and 28:25 opens on the messenger formula with the gathering of Israel, so the coda is a restoration word in its own right and is taken as its own unit; the samekh recorded after 28:24 (single witness) marks a paragraph inside that coda and decides nothing about this seam.
P06-014.device_notes: No K/Q note, paseq or editorial note falls inside 28:20-23 (single-witness apparatus), and no parashah mark is recorded on any verse of the span; the nearest marks are the pe after 28:19 and the samekh after 28:24 (single witness), one on each far face. Interior turns weighed and not taken: at 28:22 the messenger formula follows 28:21, which ends on the command to prophesy with no close formula, and it stands inside the speech that command introduces (וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ 'and say', oshb:Ezek.28.22), so it is paragraph-grade; at 28:23 no onset device follows the recognition formula of 28:22, which stands mid-verse with further clauses after it, so that turn is paragraph-grade as well.

P07-001.boundary_rationale: Onset side: the hard-seam dateline at oshb:Ezek.29.1 (year 10, month 10, day 12) uses the perfect hayah word-event form, immediately followed by the set-your-face address to Pharaoh at oshb:Ezek.29.2 and the messenger formula opening the verdict speech at oshb:Ezek.29.3 (the great-monster-in-his-rivers charge). Close side: the strict recognition formula at oshb:Ezek.29.9a closes the crocodile-verdict unit; the same verse continues with a causal clause the WEB itself paragraphs mid-verse (web:Ezek.29.9), and oshb:Ezek.29.10 opens a fresh against-you verdict cycle restating the same charge -- an onset/close collision at 29:9 -> 29:10 -- so the row seam sits at the verse boundary after 29:9, not inside it. That close has the weak shape: the recognition formula runs only to the etnachta of 29:9 and an independent causal clause with its own finite verb fills the rest of the verse, so the near face of the close is a mid-verse formula, and that is the ground for the reduced confidence the row carries.
P07-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: Three alternatives are weighed. (1) Ending the row at 29:6, where an extended (non-strict) recognition-type close occurs; rejected because 29:7 continues the same staff-of-reed image with no intervening onset, and because this chapter's own onset/close collision pattern places the true seam after 29:9, not 29:6. Two further readings are weighed. (2) Cutting at 29:7/29:8 - the alternative the paragraph layer proposes, and the witness's sectioning is disclosed for it: MEASURED, this witness places a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness) after MT 29:7, recorded on the verse it follows, and that verse additionally carries one ketiv/qere pair, already disclosed in this row. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 29:8 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.29.8), and with it a grammatical addressee shift - MT 29:7 addresses a masculine singular and MT 29:8 a feminine singular (oshb:Ezek.29.7, oshb:Ezek.29.8), that is, from Pharaoh to the land. Whether it is licensed: a messenger formula cuts as a sub-onset when its addressee differs from the one before or when the preceding verse ends on a close-role formula, and the first of those IS satisfied by that addressee change, so this rival is licensed and is not dismissed. It is one-faced: MT 29:7 ends with no close-role formula, so the second would fail there, and the SAMEKH after it (single-witness) is a mark, which makes no face. The stated ground on which this row holds: the crocodile verdict's own refrain is the recognition formula at MT 29:9, and MT 29:10 restates the same charge as a fresh against-you cycle (oshb:Ezek.29.10); since a licensed text signal takes precedence over a section mark, the SAMEKH after MT 29:7 is weak corroboration, disclosed FOR this rival and not for this row. (3) Tiling MT 29:1-29:16 as ONE row, with the mid-verse WEB paragraph at 29:9 and the forty-years turn at 29:13 falling inside it. What supports it: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, no dateline and no word-event formula stands anywhere between MT 29:1 and the next dateline at MT 29:17; MEASURED in this witness, the marks inside that stretch follow MT 29:7 (a samekh) and MT 29:12 (a pe), a further pe follows MT 29:16 at that stretch's own close and corroborates this alternative, and NO mark stands on MT 29:9 (single-witness). And this row's own close has the weak mid-verse shape: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the recognition formula in MT 29:9 ends at the etnachta and an INDEPENDENT causal clause with a finite verb fills the rest of the verse (oshb:Ezek.29.9) - unlike MT 29:6, whose words after its own recognition clause are a causal phrase built on an infinitive construct (oshb:Ezek.29.6), a dependent completion that grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal rather than the weak mid-verse shape. The stated ground on which this row holds: MT 29:10 opens a fresh against-you verdict cycle restating the charge, so the collision is resolved at the verse boundary after 29:9. The weakness of the 29:9 close and the case for a single 29:1-16 row are disclosed rather than argued away; the mid-verse close at 29:9 is the ground for the row's reduced confidence.

P07-006.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 31:9/31:10 (figure versus verdict) or 31:14/31:15 (verdict versus Sheol descent); both rejected because neither messenger-formula recurrence changes addressee and neither is preceded by a refrain close, so they mark paragraphs, not rows; the genre itself is held between an oracle against a nation and a parable-allegory, disclosed rather than resolved.
P07-006.device_notes: Length disclosed as a fact: 18 verses, against the 7-10 typical density; the length is no ground for the grade. The dated seams at both ends carry a signal on each face (the dateline and word-event at 31:1 after the verse-final recognition formula and samekh at 30:26; the utterance formula and samekh at 31:18 before the dateline at 32:1), and the reduced confidence rests on the stretch the chapter stands in: through chapters 25-32 oracle closes and fresh onsets collide and the division into units is held open, and here whether the dated cedar figure is one allegory or an oracle against Pharaoh with a figure inside it is left unresolved. K/Q at oshb:Ezek.31.5; single-witness samekh follows oshb:Ezek.31.9, oshb:Ezek.31.14 and oshb:Ezek.31.18; the closing verse oshb:Ezek.31.18 also carries two OSHB editorial notes (an accent divergence from BHS and a ketiv/qere divergence from BHS), single-witness apparatus, disclosed. Genre held between an oracle against a nation (the messenger-formula verdict structure) and a parable-allegory (the extended whom-are-you-like figure); classed here as an oracle against a nation, the deviation from the figure's own category disclosed rather than silently resolved. A samekh stands after MT 30:26, single witness, corroborating this unit's onset at 31:1. onset bytes (oshb:Ezek.31.1): וַיְהִ֗י בְּאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה בַּשְּׁלִישִׁ֖י בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר | close bytes (oshb:Ezek.31.18): אֶל מִ֨י דָמִ֥יתָ כָּ֛כָה בְּכָב֥וֹד וּבְגֹ֖דֶל בַּעֲצֵי עֵ֑דֶן וְהוּרַדְתָּ֨ אֶת עֲצֵי עֵ֜דֶן אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ תַּחְתִּ֗ית בְּת֨וֹךְ עֲרֵלִ֤ים תִּשְׁכַּב֙ אֶת חַלְלֵי חֶ֔רֶב ה֤וּא פַרְעֹה֙ וְכָל הֲמוֹנֹ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה

P08-016.boundary_rationale: Onset: 36:1 opens וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.36.1), “You, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel” (web:Ezek.36.1), turning the address from Mount Seir toward Israel's own mountains directly after 35:15 has ended verse-final on the recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.35.15), with a pe recorded after it (single witness): a signal on each face. It is a sub-onset, not a new word-event: the word-event of 35:1 is the only one that frames the oracle against Mount Seir and this address, so the seam divides one word-event unit, and that shared frame is disclosed. Close: 36:15 ends verse-final on the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.15) with a samekh after it (single witness); the verse is a ketiv/qere site, though the quoted formula does not touch the disputed word. 36:16 then opens on the strict word-event formula (oshb:Ezek.36.16): again a signal on each face. Inside the span no turn is licensed: the messenger formulae that head or fill 36:2-7 (sweep: 6 verses) keep the mountains and the land of Israel as their addressee and none follows a verse-final close formula, and the samekh after 36:4 corroborates a paragraph there without deciding it; 36:11 ends verse-final on the second-person plural recognition formula, but 36:12 opens with no onset device; 36:13's messenger formula follows 36:12, which ends with no close-role formula and has a samekh after it, and it keeps the land as its addressee while the address moves from masculine to feminine singular, a paragraph-grade turn (the addressee is a reading on the measured forms). The faces alone would carry more; the row is held at reduced confidence because the one word-event of 35:1 frames 35:1-36:15 as a single unit, so the standing of this half-chapter as a unit of its own is an open question, and its length, 15 verses against the 7-10 typical density, is disclosed as a fact.
P08-016.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 35:1-36:15 as one unit under the single word-event of 35:1, so that the oracle against Mount Seir and this address to Israel's mountains stand together: nothing between 35:1 and 36:16 carries a second word-event. Weighed and not taken: 35:15 closes the oracle against Mount Seir verse-final on the recognition formula with a pe after it (single witness), and 36:1's 'and you, son of man' turns the address from Seir toward Israel's mountains, which licenses a sub-onset at 36:1; the shared frame is disclosed rather than cut away, and it is why the row carries reduced confidence.
P08-016.device_notes: The burden of the span is the restoration of the mountains of Israel, the tilling, sowing and multiplying of 36:8-11 and the promise that the land will no longer bereave its people (36:12-15), rather than a verdict against a foreign nation, so it is classed as a salvation oracle; the oracle-against-a-nation reading that the shared frame with 35:1-15 might suggest is disclosed and not taken, since the addressee is Israel's own territory. From 36:13 the address shifts toward the land in the feminine singular, in a verse that still carries a masculine-plural 'to you' (לָכֶ֔ם, oshb:Ezek.36.13). The ketiv/qere apparatus carries five notes inside the span, two at 36:13, two at 36:14 and one at 36:15 (single-witness apparatus); each is disclosed in the entries for those verses and none is argued for a boundary. Paseq is recorded within 36:5 and 36:6, one stroke each (count-only, single witness; the position within the verse is not stated). An editors' note on 36:7 records an accent reading in L that differs from BHS (single-witness apparatus), disclosed and not argued. Interior turns weighed and not taken: 36:12/36:13 (a messenger formula after a verse without a close formula, the land still addressed) and 36:11/36:12 (a verse-final recognition with no onset device after it) are both paragraph-grade, and the verse-final utterance formula of 36:14 is followed by 36:15 with no onset device, so the close falls a verse later.

P09-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: the verse opens on the hand-of-YHWH idiom immediately followed by a transport verb, oshb:Ezek.37.1 הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֨וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת -- the same onset shape that opens the book's other three long prose visions, and this occurrence is one of only 7 hand-of-YHWH verses in the book. The unit is held as one scene, with the live rival inside it weighed below: the prophet is set down among the bones (37.1-2), questioned and commanded to prophesy twice -- once to the bones, once to the breath/spirit (37.4-6, 37.9), watches the two-stage reanimation (37.7-8, 37.10), and receives the scene's own interpretation as a word to 'son of man' (oshb:Ezek.37.11 וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ). Close: oshb:Ezek.37.14 stacks three refrain-grade closes in one verse -- the second-person plural recognition variant (the 'you shall know that I am YHWH' form, part of a 21-verse 2mp family sweep), the emphatic 'I YHWH have spoken' close (one of 14 book-wide), and the short utterance signature without the divine-name pair (one of only 4 such short forms in the book) -- וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֞ם כִּי אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִׂ֖יתִי נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and a pe mark is recorded immediately after this verse (single-witness, informing not deciding). Both sides of the following seam were weighed: oshb:Ezek.37.15 opens with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, one of 39 verses carrying that strict form, so the close at 37.14 and the fresh onset at 37.15 corroborate each other from both directions. Both faces of that close carry full signals; what keeps the row from the highest confidence is a licensed rival inside the span, at the 37.10/37.11 seam, held on stated grounds.
P09-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at the two samekh-marked points inside the scene: after the army stands up at oshb:Ezek.37.10, and after the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.37.12 (single-witness marks on both). The first is a real and licensed rival: 37.11 opens on a he-said-to-me clause with the son-of-man address (sweep: 93 verses book-wide), a default onset inside a vision, with the samekh standing behind it on 37.10 -- so 37.1-10 would be a complete scene (the question, the command to prophesy, and the army that stands up as its result) and 37.11-14 its interpretation, which carries a messenger formula of its own at 37.12 and a recognition close. It is not taken because 37.1-14 is held as one vision report; the other he-said-to-me verses inside the scene (37.3, 37.4, 37.9) are onset-type devices inside the vision, each a licensed alternative, held because the question, the two commands and their two results form one scene and 37.1-14 stands whole as the vision, and the transport at 37.2 would leave a one-verse remainder. That licensed rival at 37.10/37.11 is what keeps this row from the highest confidence; which of the recognition clauses at 37.6, 37.13 and 37.14 closes the row is held open here.

The faces alone would carry more: the onset follows the verse-final recognition formula of 38.23 with a samekh after it, and the close is the verse-final utterance formula of 39.10 with a samekh after it (single witness for both marks), though 39.11 opens with no onset device; it is the open question at the onset, stated here as the row's own ground, that holds the row at the lowest grade. 39.9 carries one paseq (count-only, single-witness) inside this span.

P09-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: no word-event, messenger, hand-of-YHWH or address formula opens 39:21, whose near face therefore carries no device of any tracked class, and the single witness records no mark at 39:20 either; the seam rests on the verse-final utterance signature at 39:20, which stands there alone, and on the topical turn from the birds-and-beasts summons to a first-person retrospective on Israel's exile. Inside that retrospective the wide-family recognition close addressed to “the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.39.22) stands at 39.22, one of the expansions in the 64-verse wide sweep and not the strict 28, and is internal, paragraph-final rather than row-final; 39.23 is no second such close -- its knowing-clause carries no divine-name predicate and belongs to no tracked class. The onset at 39:21 is thus a topical turn without any onset device, and the Gog chapters 38-39, where recapitulation and sequence remain an open question, are held at reduced confidence as a stretch; both are the ground for the confidence this row carries. Close side: 43:12 closes on a doubled envelope formula, זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת ... הִנֵּה זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.43.12) “This is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12) ... “Behold, this is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12), repeating the title at the top and bottom of the same verse -- a strong lexical close-device, and the reason this three-verse span is held as its own row despite its length: the inclusio is a self-contained frame around 43:10-12 that a larger row would have to break through rather than around. The grade rests on these faces: the onset is a turn to the prophet without a counted device, since 43:10's address lacks the conjunction of the counted family, after a samekh on 43:9 that is no signal of its own; the close is the genre colophon in the composition's own voice, and its far face at 43:13 opens the altar's measurements with a list heading, which carries no signal on a far face; the stretch from the glory's return to the torah of the house is one whose division into units is held open, which keeps the row at reduced confidence and no lower.

P11-007.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at Ezek.46.1 opens the Sabbath/new-moon gate rule, itself carrying “the day of the new moon” (web:Ezek.46.1) -- disclosed as a chodesh-root homograph, not a date formula (recurring at 46.6); the construction glossed 'at the new moons' recurs at 46.3, the same homograph family as Ezek.45.17. The unit runs through the prince's Sabbath offering (4-8), the people's festival entry-and-exit rule (9-10), the feast-day meal offering (11-12), and the daily burnt offering (13-15), where Ezek.46.13's 'a lamb of its first year' carries a year word that is explicitly NOT a dateline. The messenger formula at 46:1 is the division set at the head of the chapter, where the law section is divided on its messenger formulae, so the onset is not in question; the reduced confidence rests on the close: 46:15 ends the daily burnt offering with no close-role formula, and the pe recorded after it (single witness) corroborates the paragraph without deciding it. A samekh mark is also recorded after Ezek.46.11 (single witness), mid-unit; it is weighed and disclosed but does not cut, since no messenger-formula or addressee-class change corroborates a seam there -- the next messenger formula is not until 46.16, past the end of this row -- and a parashah mark unaccompanied by a text signal never decides a boundary alone.

P11-014.boundary_rationale: Onset: no formula device opens Ezek.48.8; the seam at 48.7/48.8 rests instead on the northern block's own close (the 'one portion' refrain at 48.7) and a change of listed object -- from tribal portions to the holy offering itself. The row covers the dimensions of the holy portion given to the sanctuary, priests and Levites (8-14), the remaining strip for the city and its common land (15-19), the whole square portion set apart with the sanctuary at its centre (20), and the prince's land on either side of the holy portion and the city, framed by Judah's and Benjamin's borders (21-22). A samekh mark is recorded after Ezek.48.11, mid-unit, inside the priests' portion; disclosed, but it does not cut, since it is unaccompanied by any change of addressee or genre and the holy-portion description continues without a fresh onset. Paseq is recorded within Ezek.48.18 (one), Ezek.48.21 (three) and Ezek.48.22 (one), count-only, single-witness; five K/Q sites fall inside the row, at 48:14, 48:15, 48:16, 48:18 and 48:21 (single-witness apparatus), none argued for a boundary. Close: the next verse, 48.23, reopens the tribal-portion list on its own resumption formula, a change of listed object back from the holy portion, city and prince to the southern tribes -- a real content seam at the list's internal division, formula-free like this row's own onset.
P11-014.device_notes: Neither this row's onset at 48.8 nor its close before 48.23 carries a formula device; both are argued from a change of listed object, disclosed as such. The samekh recorded after Ezek.48.11 is single-witness, mid-unit, non-cutting. Held at reduced confidence because both seams rest on a change of listed object with no formula on either near face.
